model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent win: a D+6 seat, an 8-point favorable environment, and Bera's overwhelming cash advantage against a challenger with almost no money. Prediction markets on both major platforms price Bera's win probability at 94-95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing the race inside single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Ami Bera, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored in this Sacramento-area district that leans Democratic by about six points. The national environment also favors his party this cycle, adding to an already solid structural advantage. Bera has raised $1.25 million and holds $1.8 million in cash, while Republican Robb Tucker has raised roughly $258,000 and reports only $16,000 on hand, leaving him little capacity to compete on the airwaves.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have listed the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and money. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Bera's chances in the mid-90s, in line with a Safe D assessment. Tucker would need a dramatic, well-funded shift to make this competitive.
